sub_palette: near_eastern (old_persian) backbone + east_asian (japonic) overlay (cross-family blend, Persian-leaning)

blend.backbone: near_eastern (old_persian register: the Xshayathiya/satrapal court, the ezafe genitive-of-relation, Arta the right-order, theophoric -data/-farnah names, spirant th/x/f, the paridaida rose-garden, SOV with heavy-syllable stress)
blend.overlay: east_asian (japonic: the shrine-isle and the kami, open CV moras, the -no- honorific link, rendaku voicing, castle-towns and daimyo houses, the disciplined warrior-way, native island/shrine/material vocabulary)
blend.lean: Persian-heavy - an Old Persian satrapal court enthroned over the Japonic shrine-isles: the King of Kings and his satraps hold the rose-garden court and the road, the island clans and their kami-shrines endure and serve beneath; the ezafe meets the honorific bow.

_note: NEW cross-family hybrid under the base/hybrid model. BASE_04 Axsatra (Old Persian / Achaemenid) x BASE_08 Yamatai (Japonic / Sengoku Japan). CIV/CLAN DECIDED by inheritance: Persian base = Civilized, Japonic base = Clanhold, and any Civ parent -> Civ, so Hinostan is Civilized (feudal). Concept: a Perso-Japonic realm - the rose-garden court and the shrine-isle as one, the ezafe and the honorific bow. An Old Persian court-aristocracy (a Shah-house with its satraps) enthroned over the Japonic island-clans and their kami-shrines; the Persian register rules, the island populace and its shrine-craft endure and serve beneath. Backbone = Old Persian (the satrapal/court register, Arta the right-order, theophoric -data/-farnah names, the ezafe); overlay/substrate = Japonic (the shrine-isles, the kami, the castle-towns, the warrior-clans, the material/staple words). Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Old-Persian and Japanese registers (allowed, catalog 5.3); DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon from both parents (Persian-shifted canon morphs PRIMARY per axsatran, Japonic native kami-morphs SECONDARY per yamataian/family_east_asian.japonic), never real gods or kami. All human cultures allow Lawful/Neutral/Chaotic. Ruler/domain DISPLAY titles are English (or an approved commonly-known foreign term); conlang titles moved to ruler_native/domain_native for NPC dialogue. APPROVED FOREIGN TERM: kingdom display = 'Shah' (the commonly-known Persian sovereign-title); duchy display = 'Daimyo' (the commonly-known Japanese great-lord title for the island satrap-houses). Both recorded in approved_foreign_terms_used.

phonology.palette: Old Persian (Indo-Iranian) backbone - vowels a i u with long a/i/u; spirants th(0)/x(kh)/f; sibilants s/sh/z/c(ts); r l; nasals m n; semivowels y v/w; aspirate h; clusters xsh-, sp-, st-, fr-, vr-, thr-; the ezafe genitive-of-relation '-ahya'; theophoric on the Persian-shifted canon morphs (Turvasa-, Urlaspa-, Arta-, Baga-) - meeting a Japonic overlay: open CV moras (only coda -n), five vowels a i u e o, rendaku (sequential voicing) in compounds, the -no- honorific link, kami honorifics. Per the CSV: a mora-timed rhythm carried on poetic Persian meter; the Japonic CV syllables flow into Persian long vowels and the ezafe; grammar is SOV with an honorific ezafe (the Persian construct fused with the Japonic -no- bow). Theophoric on the Persian reflexes (Turvasa-, Urlaspa-) with Japonic kami-variants (-no-kami).
phonology.phonotactics: CV(C) leaning to the Persian; Persian clusters (xsh-, sp-, st-, fr-, thr-) admitted at word-head while medial syllables open into Japonic CV moras; vowel length distinctive; stress on heavy syllables with a mora-counted poetic pull; the ezafe '-ahya' / '-e' links elements where Japonic would use -no-.

sound_changes: Japonic open CV-moras adapted to Persian flowing vowels: terminal moras shed or lengthen (-a/-i/-u absorbed into Persian long vowels), -e/-o raised toward Persian a/i/u except where a signature mora is kept; final vowel may drop before a Persian consonant-cluster ending
Japonic rendaku voicing yields to Persian spirantization: medial -k->-x-/-g-, -t->-th-/-d-, -s->-sh-/-z- where the Persian phonology pulls; Japonic -ts-/-ch- collapse to Persian c/sh
the linking particle fuses: Japonic -no- and Persian ezafe '-ahya' merge into the honorific ezafe '-e'/'-ahya' that binds compounds and relation
Persian heavy-syllable / poetic-meter stress imposed on all words; Persian word-head clusters (xsh-, sp-, st-, fr-, thr-) permitted; the long vowels carry the meter

retain Persian th, x, f, the ezafe and the -arta/-farnah/-data endings, and a few Japonic signatures (the -shima isle-mora, the -no-kami shrine-honorific, open final vowels on island/staple roots); very short roots take a Persian -a
fusion_rules.source_tilt: island/shrine/material/staple words from Japonic roots (the island substrate works the land, tends the shrine and the rice); rule/kin-line/court/land/abstract/war words from Old Persian roots (the ruling court register); every root then filtered to the one Persian-shaped phonology

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Japonic island/shrine/material/staple-roots + Old Persian rule/kin/court/land-roots, all run through one Persian-shaped sound-law (open Japonic moras flowing into Persian long vowels and the ezafe, rendaku yielding to spirantization); portmanteaus mark the blended institutions and bloodline.

morphology.patronymic_form: the Persian court-stock keep filiation 'X-ahya musuthra' (son of X) or compact 'X-musuthra' and a house (ujith-X); the Japonic island-clans keep the clan-name (uji) first with the honorific ezafe '-e' (X-e-Y, the fused -no-) and a fief-name; theophoric given names on the Persian-shifted god-stems and on Arta- (Truth); the throne fuses both - a Shah who also carries an island ujith-house.
morphology.compounding_rule: quality/relation + element via the honorific ezafe '-e'/'-ahya' (fusing the Persian construct and the Japonic -no-): Arta-xshaca (truth-realm), Kura-shirda (black-castle, rendaku yielded to the Persian shape), Niwaida-e-Riyata (the rose-garden of Riyata); toponyms Dida-[name] (fort of), [name]-pura (city of), [name]-jinjana (shrine-town of), [name]-shima (the isle of).

title_ladder.government: feudal (an Old Persian court-aristocracy over the Japonic shrine-isles: the Xshayathiya/Shah and his vispuhra-kin at the rose-garden court, the satraps (Xshacapavan) holding the great island-provinces as daimyo-houses, the vispati clan-lords sworn beneath; the island shugo-governors and the kannushi shrine-priesthood serve under the Persian crown)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Old Persian ladder, ascending, with the Japonic island substrate co-titles fused beneath. Vispati (clan-lord of a vis) barony; Marzapana (march-warden, the marzban) march; Shugva (province-governor; Japonic shugo shifted to the Persian shape) county over a Kunva (the island kuni-province); Xshacapavan (SATRAP, protector of the realm), shown as DAIMYO in display, duchy over a satrapy (the great island-provinces held as daimyo-houses); Vispuhra (prince of the blood) principality over a Dahyu (great province); Xshayathiya (king), shown as SHAH in display, kingdom over a Xshacam; Xshayathiya Xshayathiyanam (King of Kings) empire over the Vispa-Dahyu, all the lands. The island clans keep their shugo (governor) and kannushi (shrine-priest) beneath the Persian crown. The magu-priests of the fire and the kannushi of the kami stand outside the ladder. Rank titles fuse the real Old-Persian and Japanese registers (allowed); display titles are English save the approved foreign terms Shah (kingdom) and Daimyo (duchy).

title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH, save the two approved commonly-known foreign terms set in 'ruler': Shah (kingdom) and Daimyo (duchy). The *_native conlang forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: the Persian court-stock carry a given (often theophoric or Arta-/Vahu- virtue-name) + filiation (X-musuthra) and a house (ujith-X); the Japonic island-clans carry the clan-name (uji) first linked by the honorific ezafe '-e' to a given name; order given-first for the court, clan-first for the isles.
people_name_convention.dual_register: the Persian court-and-satrapal nobility carry a house (ujith) and a satrapal office; the Japonic island warrior-clans (the buke) carry a clan-name + military title; commoners use filiation or a single island-name + earned epithet.
people_name_convention.theophoric: court given names from the Persian-shifted deity-stems + an Old Persian element: Baga-X (god-X), X-data (X-given), X-farnah (glory-of-X), Vahu-X (good-X), e.g. Turvasa-data, Baga-Urlaspa, Artafarnah; island names invoke the native kami + an element: -maru (child/blade), Take- (valor), and the -no-kami / fused -e-kami devotional, e.g. Takebimaru, names honoring Terashi-no-kami.

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Persian-shifted canon morphs PRIMARY (axsatran's Old-Persian-shifted set, the Turvasa/Urlaspa column) with Japonic native kami-morphs SECONDARY (family_east_asian.json theonym_sets.japonic, the -no-kami set) - recognizably the same powers under two faces (a Perso-Japonic honji-suijaku: the Persian yazata and the island kami are one power, two faces), never real Iranian/Zoroastrian gods or Shinto kami. Lawful henotheist but TOLERANT in the Persian manner: Asturna the Wise Lord most high upholds ARTA (Truth/Right-order) and the Lawful powers are His yazata-ministers (and the islands' bright kami His shrine-faces); the Chaotic powers are the hosts of DRAUGA (the Lie) and the wild island oni. The cardinal sin is the Lie; the Shah's word is bond. The empire shelters the island shrine-cults under Asturna's peace - the kami are honored, never suppressed.
religion.the_one: Asturna (< Aeternus / Sargonid Itarnu; the Wise Lord Most High, upholder of Arta and source of the Shah's farnah-glory; the islands name His high face Takami-no-kami, the High-Heaven One above the myriad kami)

sample_deity_renames.Tulrius: Turvasa (the sun and Arta, lamp of right-order; island face Terashi-no-kami, the Shining One; Lawful)
sample_deity_renames.Orlandus: Urlaspa (the iron-oath, war and the cavalier; island face Hagane-no-kami, the Steel One; Lawful)
sample_deity_renames.Numeno: Naumana (the good mind, wisdom and the law; island face Amatsukaze-no-kami; Lawful)
sample_deity_renames.Gaiandus: Gayanta (the enduring earth and mountain; island face Iwane-no-kami, the Rock-Root)
sample_deity_renames.Realta: Riyata (the Lady of Waters, mother and mercy; island face Megumi-hime, the Mercy-Maiden)

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers - Asturna upholding Arta, Turvasa the just, Urlaspa of the sworn oath, Riyata the merciful - and their bright island shrine-faces (Terashi-no-kami, Hagane-no-kami); names the Chaotic powers the hosts of Drauga the Lie and the wild oni, warded; the Persian fire-altar and the island kami-shrine bind alike under the Shah's right-order.
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: the honest dead kept as fravashi (fore-spirits) and the ancestral kami of the island clans (the senzo enshrined at the household jinjana); the great powers and the place-kami invoked at the fire-altar and the shrine-grove situationally.
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon, the hosts of Drauga and the wild war-fury of the storm-kami and the mountain-oni, and names the Lawful powers - and Asturna - the tyrant-lords of a false order to be defied.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers, warded as the hosts of Drauga the Lie (Persian) or as wild oni (Japonic island), keep their morphs + a hostile epithet: Maraxus -> Marakhsha the Burner-of-Cities (island face Takebi-no-kami the War-Flame); Vacidus -> Vakida the Devouring-Void (island Utsuro-no-kami); Lusanto -> Lusanta the Coin-Serpent (island Kogane-Orochi the gold hoard-serpent).

clergy_ladder.5: Magupati (chief magus of a fire-temple) / Negi (senior priest)
clergy_ladder.9: Magupatan Magupat (the chief of chief magi) / Saishu (high priest of the realm)

religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Atash ([fire] of [power]) and its fire-temple (Atashana) for the court powers - 'the Atashana of Turvasa'; the Jinjana (kami-fire shrine-town) of [power] for the island faces - 'the Jinjana of Terashi-no-kami', within its torii and sacred grove; the two named as one power, two faces.
religion.saints_pattern: the honest dead and the just Shahs kept as fravashi (fore-spirits) at the fire-altar - 'the Arta-true [name]'; and the great island ancestors and fallen heroes enshrined as kami (the eirei) at the clan jinjana - 'the kami [name]'.

holy_symbol_motifs.Asturna: a winged ring-disc (the farnah-glory) above a fire-altar set before a torii
holy_symbol_motifs.Turvasa: a rayed sun above the upright Arta-measure and a mirror
holy_symbol_motifs.Urlaspa: an iron spear crossed with an oath-ring before a bare blade

banks_patterns.dungeons_ruins: fallen apadana-halls and abandoned island jinjana: 'the dead Atashana of [name]', 'the haunted Jinjana of [clan]', 'the buried Apadana of Dida-[name]'
